subject: How to interpret RI-CLPM parameter estimates when variables means decrease over time

messages.author: 92e95a2e289fb891
messages.subject: How to interpret RI-CLPM parameter estimates when variables means decrease over time
parts:
Hi there, I ran an RI-CLPM model over 4 time points, with cross-lagged parameter constrained to be equal across time. Results suggested that higher within-person X at previous time point predicted higher within-person Y at subsequent time point (positive relationship). However, when looking at the descriptive statistics of my sample, the overall means of X and Y decrease over time (possibly due to regression to the mean or an effect of being assessed).

With regard to my interpretations given the overall means, can I still say that when a person reports more X (e.g., negative social interactions) than they usually do, they also report more Y (e.g., depression) than they usually do later on, so an exacerbation effect. OR is the correct interpretation given that the sample means of X (negative social interactions) and Y (depression) seem to go down over time (e.g., a sort of recovery effect), that a "positive" cross-lagged path is actually showing some sort of stunting of this recovery effect.
